That record is checked by the duplicate detection component against existing Xero records before being handed to the approval routing engine, which determines the required approver(s) based on department and the £10,000/£50,000 thresholds. The notification component sends the approval request and captures the response; if no response arrives within a defined window, the escalation/reminder component fires reminders and can escalate. Approval status feeds a dashboard for visibility at every stage. {"factors":[{"factor":"workflow","score":4,"justification":"The design has multiple sequential stages (intake, extraction, duplicate check, routing, notification, escalation, dashboard, posting) plus conditional branching on department and two amount thresholds (£10,000 and £50,000) and a time-based escalation loop for stalled approvals, which is more than moderate branching but not deeply nested or parallel."},{"factor":"integration","score":3,"justification":"The architecture connects three distinct systems: the email mailbox (intake and approver communication), a data extraction capability, and Xero as system of record. These are conventional interfaces (email, accounting API) rather than many heterogeneous or poorly documented systems."},{"factor":"data_logic","score":4,"justification":"The Invoice Data Extraction component must reshape unstructured PDFs into structured fields including UK VAT handling, and the Approval Routing Engine must apply interacting department/amount rules; combined with duplicate-detection matching logic (left unspecified), this is a dense rule set beyond simple mapping."},{"factor":"failure_risk","score":4,"justification":"Duplicate payments have already occurred three times, approval responses can be lost with no visibility, and posting to Xero must not silently fail; the design requires deliberate handling (manual review queues, retries, stale-state marking) across several distinct failure modes with real financial consequence."},{"factor":"operational","score":3,"justification":"Low-confidence extractions, ambiguous duplicate matches, and unmapped department/amount combinations are routed to manual review, implying periodic staff attention and rule maintenance (e.g., as department/approver mappings evolve), though nothing suggests continuous specialist monitoring."}]}
